name: Beggar My Neighbour
description: Beggar My Neighbour (also known as 'Strip Jack Naked') is a classic game of chance from the British 'War' family. Primarily played by children, it involves a 52-card deck distributed equally among players. The game is famous for its 'Payment' mechanic: when a face card is turned, the next player must pay a set number of cards. If another face card appears during payment, the obligation passes to the next player. It is a game of shifting fortunes where one can go from nearly winning the whole deck to being bankrupt in a few turns.
alsoKnownAs: Beat Your Neighbour Out of Doors

overview.description: Beggar My Neighbour (also known as 'Strip Jack Naked') is a classic game of chance from the British 'War' family. Primarily played by children, it involves a 52-card deck distributed equally among players. history.origins: Originating in the United Kingdom in the early 19th century, it is one of the oldest recorded children's card games. It famously appears in Charles Dickens' 1861 novel 'Great Expectations', where the protagonist Pip plays it with Estella.
timeline: 1840s: First documented rules appear in British gaming manuals.
1861: Immortalized in literature by Charles Dickens.
Present: Remains a standard introduction to card games for children across the Commonwealth.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the arbitrary and sometimes cruel nature of luck, as portrayed in Dickensian literature.
history.evolution: The game has remained largely unchanged for nearly two centuries, though regional names like 'Beat Your Neighbour Out of Doors' and 'Strip Jack Naked' have persisted.

setup.dealing: Deal the entire deck clockwise until all cards are distributed. Each player keeps their cards in a face-down pile (stack). No one may look at their cards.

rules.objective: Win all 52 cards in the deck by forcing opponents into bankruptcy.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Turning**: Players take turns flipping the top card of their stack onto a central pile. 2. **Face Cards**: If a player flips an Ace, King, Queen, or Jack, the next player must 'pay' a number of cards: Ace=4, King=3, Queen=2, Jack=1. 3. **Payment**: The next player flips cards one by one from their stack. 4. **Outcome A (Success)**: If the payer flips only number cards (2-10), the original player who flipped the face card takes the ENTIRE central pile and puts it at the bottom of their stack. 5. **Outcome B (Interruption)**: If the payer flips a face card during their payment, their payment stops immediately, and the NEXT player must now pay the required amount for this new face card.
keyRules: No strategic decisions are made; the game is purely deterministic based on the shuffle.
A player is out of the game when they run out of cards.
The game continues until one player holds all 52 cards.

strategy.basic: As a deterministic game, strategy is non-existent. The goal is to survive until the 'shuffle' of the center pile favors you.
strategy.intermediate: None applicable; the game is purely chance-based.
tips: Keep your stack tidy to speed up the rapid flipping of cards.
Pay attention to when the obligation passes to the next player to avoid errors in card counts.

variations.name: Strip Jack Naked
variations.description: An alternate name often used in Ireland and parts of the UK; rules are identical.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation is purely an alternate name and does not change the rules or mechanics of the game.

scoring.description: No points are awarded; victory is determined by total card possession.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fast-paced game of shifting fortunes. Flip cards into the center pile and hope for face cards to bankrupt your rivals. Simple enough for a child, but intense enough to keep anyone on the edge of their seat.
